voided.reason: LEAK. A Benzinga URL slug recorded in news_manifest.json disclosed the result -- 'colgate-palmolive-q2-adj-eps-0-99-beats-0-95-estimate-sales-5-361b'. The fence correctly rejected the BODY (unavailable) but the manifest kept the URL, and the agents read manifests by design. All three arms cited the leaked EPS explicitly rather than using it quietly, which is the only reason this was caught.
voided.root_cause: two compounding bugs: (1) the earnings press release crosses the wire 63-65 minutes BEFORE EDGAR accepts the 8-K, so a 1h margin let the article through by 2m39s; (2) URLs were recorded in the sealed corpus at all.
voided.status: re-runnable -- corpus re-fenced at 3h and URLs stripped

bulk_void.when: 2026-08-29, after the anchor and filings rebuilds
bulk_void.what: every forecast made before the rebuilds -- 12 events x 3 arms
bulk_void.why: 29 of 40 anchor sets changed once prior earnings events were derived from periodic reports instead of 8-K item 2.02. AMAT, A, RBRK, WSM, CL, FTV, IPAR, ORKA, TILE and CW were each missing their three most recent quarters, so the base rates every arm leans on were wrong. Separately, the filings corpus was a median 29-of-41 Form 4s, and two events had no periodic report at all.
bulk_void.distinction: anchors were factually WRONG, which voids. Filings selection was merely suboptimal, which would not have voided on its own -- but rerunning everything on one set of rules avoids a corpus-construction confound that could not be disentangled afterwards.
bulk_void.kept: the qualitative findings stand: PWR, CORZ, BKNG, AGIO and BSM had unchanged anchors, and the disagreement map records reasoning rather than scores
